item: A route's slowest call says how long it spent before routing handed it to its endpoint (before_dispatch_ms)
summary: The middleware stamps the moment it first sees a request and an async application-level dependency stamps the moment routing hands it to its endpoint (async so it takes no thread of the pool it measures); the difference rides on the route's slowest call in request-latency.json. None (never 0) where either stamp is missing or out of order. Found because GET /api/scheduler/status costs 0.65 ms in its handler against a 67 ms p50 in the field: the time is outside the handler, and this says which side of the hand-off it was on. The figure includes the framework reading the request body (it does that before it resolves dependencies), so a slow upload counts as time before dispatch; it is None when the two clocks disagree (the split would exceed the request's own duration). What remains of ms is the endpoint's thread wait, its run and the response, not split further. The dependency takes an HTTPConnection so a future WebSocket route is not broken by it. About 28 B per route row. A stall-record patch for OSM's file is in rc-diagnostics/dispatch-split-2026-10-17/.
